claim: Cueing a memory during slow-wave/NREM sleep gives a small, reliable memory gain in humans (g about 0.29 pooled; about 0.18 after publication-bias correction).
agent_test: Replay a stored episode's key facts into the agent context at an idle step versus no replay, equal total tokens; measure later recall on held-out questions.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The TMR benefit is stage-specific: present in NREM/SWS, absent in REM and wake.
agent_test: Compare replay during an offline consolidation step against replay inserted mid-task (wake-like) at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: TMR effects are heterogeneous and partly fragile: I2 71 percent, funnel asymmetry, unpublished studies ns, founding skill result near zero, and a 2025 nap TMR null.
agent_test: No test needed; use it to set low expectations and require a no-replay control in every test.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Causal link: boosting slow oscillations (tES 2006, closed-loop audio 2013) raised memory in the original studies, but the closed-loop audio result failed to replicate (Henin 2019, Bayes factors 0.25 to 0.30 for equality). Gap search 2026-10: the 2021 Sleep meta-analysis gives g 0.25 (p 0.07, 177 people); a 2022 meta-analysis with g 0.68 was retracted in 2026; two more closed-loop nulls (N 27 and 34); the frontocortical tDCS study (N 20) was null overall and impaired memory only in a high-Raven subgroup; the mouse study failed to beat sham and showed about 1 s ripple suppression after each pulse.
agent_test: Not directly testable on an LLM; treat 'timing of replay matters' as unproven for the agent.

claim: Replay timed to the slow-oscillation UP state cut overnight forgetting more than DOWN-state cueing (5 vs 15 percent, N=24, re-checked), but UP did not differ from uncued.
agent_test: Analogue: consolidate at task boundaries versus mid-task; one human study only, low priority.

claim: Precise slow-oscillation and spindle coupling relates to retention across individuals, but the link is small (pooled r about 0.07, 23 studies, 297 effect sizes) and correlational.
agent_test: None; mechanism-level only. The four lines are one meta-analysis.

claim: Hippocampal reactivation of waking activity during sleep (place-cell co-firing, cortex-hippocampus coordinated replay) and ripple elimination impairing spatial memory support the replay premise in rodents.
agent_test: None for the agent; this is the biological premise. Abstract-level only here.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 0 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Sleep consolidation has a capacity limit: benefit at 160 word pairs but not at 320 (n=101); authors say the effect is near the limit of what that N can detect.
agent_test: Vary the number of episodes in the offline pass (40/160/320 analogue) and check whether rule-extraction quality saturates at fixed tokens.

claim: Sleep promotes qualitative reorganisation (gist, rule insight, inference) in humans, but support is inconsistent across labs and paradigms. Wagner 2004 exact: 59 percent (13/22) after sleep vs 22.7-25 percent in four control groups, chi2 10.2, p .03. Later: N1 helps (N 103, 83 vs 30 percent), N2 helps (N 90, 85.7 vs 55.5 percent), no benefit on insight problems and magic tricks (N 77), puzzle solving 62 vs 24 percent with no TMR gain, pink noise did not help (N 72).
agent_test: Offline pass that writes rules from episodes versus an offline pass that only stores summaries; test on questions requiring the rule, at equal tokens.

claim: Sleep deprivation after learning impairs memory only modestly (g 0.28), less than before learning (g 0.62); both subject to publication bias.
agent_test: None; sets a prior that the offline step is worth small, not large, gains.

claim: The DRM meta-analysis (Newbury & Monaghan 2019) found no overall effect of sleep on accurate or false memory, with sleep effects only emerging with moderators such as shorter lists and recall rather than recognition tests; an adapted follow-up of the authors' own 2017 visual-gist protocol (Lutz et al. 2026, N=16) found no gist difference between sleep and wake, so these two sources do not show a reliable sleep effect on DRM gist.
agent_test: Warns that gist compression may add false details; check gist-compressed memory for invented facts.
audit_note: Newbury & Monaghan 2019 found no overall sleep effect but moderated effects (list length, recall>recognition); Lutz et al. (J Sleep Res 2026) is an adapted, not direct, replication of their 2017 protocol (N=16, 12 at one year, 2 excluded from sleep analyses) and tests visual gist, not word-list DRM.
claim_before_audit: DRM false-memory/gist evidence does not show a reliable sleep effect (meta-analysis null overall; a 2026 own-lab replication of a sleep-gist effect failed with N=16).

claim: Sleep preferentially strengthens well-connected items in a learned graph (N=19 analysed, p near .04 to .05).
agent_test: Prioritise replay of high-connectivity (hub) facts versus uniform replay at equal tokens.

claim: In targeted reactivation, item-level detail falls while category-level information is preserved, linked to REM theta/beta power; this challenges an SWS-only abstraction story.
agent_test: Keep raw episodes alongside abstractions; compare abstraction-only versus abstraction plus raw store.

claim: Competing view: sleep acts through global synaptic downscaling rather than only active replay; current theory merges both.
agent_test: Test a forgetting/pruning step separately from a replay/abstraction step in an offline pass (ablation).

claim: Offline precomputation over a known context before the query cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy (Stateful GSM-Symbolic, Stateful AIME) and gives up to +13 and +18 percent with more offline compute. Re-checked against the paper.
agent_test: Direct: pre-think over the context in an idle step versus spending the same tokens at query time; benchmarks are the authors own.

claim: Sleep-time compute helps most when the query is predictable from the context, and at large test-time budgets the test-time-only baseline can win.
agent_test: Split test items by predictability; the offline pass should help the predictable half more.

claim: An offline step that reorganises, merges and abstracts agent memory improves memory-agent benchmarks at much smaller memory banks and query-time cost (LightMem, Auto-Dreamer, RecMem, All-Mem). The offline step's own token cost is mostly not charged, and the one deduplicate-only design (Microsoft, LongMemEval) only reaches parity with raw retrieval.
agent_test: Offline consolidation of episodes into a smaller rule set versus append-only memory, at equal tokens, on ALFWorld/ScienceWorld-style tasks; seed variance required.

claim: Most of the compaction in Auto-Dreamer comes from region rewriting before any training; abstraction can lose specifics (look_at_obj_in_light family).
agent_test: Keep source-linked raw episodes; test whether abstraction drops dates and locations.

claim: Gist compression drops dates: temporal preservation 3.05 percent without a fix, so gist beats truncation on multi-hop but fails on temporal questions.
agent_test: Add a rule 'preserve time, place, numbers' to the consolidation prompt and measure temporal question accuracy.

claim: Replay-priority rules (consolidate only on recurrence) cut construction cost 71 to 87 percent without accuracy loss on LoCoMo/LongMemEval. Caveat: RecMem's gating is bundled with a three-tier design; its no-gating variant scores 74.22 vs 81.10 (read from a figure). RPMem (parametric) shows a learned write gate beats fixed merges by 31.31 pp.
agent_test: Recurrence-gated versus every-turn consolidation at equal token budget.

claim: Reconsolidation after retrieval adds about +2 points on LoCoMo and LongMemEval; small and single-run. Counter-evidence: in a nine-configuration LongMemEval ablation, adding reconsolidation to dedup gave 75.8 vs 76.8 (CIs overlap fully), so the +2 is not reproduced there.
agent_test: Update memory entries at use time versus never; expect gains near 2 points, so many seeds are needed.

claim: Sleep-like replay in small neural nets (noise-driven, local rules) restores old tasks after sequential training (CIFAR-10 19.0 to 44.6; re-checked against paper), with recovery shrinking as tasks pile up and a cost to the newest task.
agent_test: Weight-level; not applicable to a scaffold-only agent. Informative trade-off: recovering old items costs newest-item accuracy.
audit_note: Numbers match Tadros 2022 (CIFAR-10 19.01 to 44.55; CUB-200 new-task 95.41 to 45.4), but the 2026 follow-up (A. Bazhenov, Delanois, Krishnan) shares Krishnan with Tadros et al. and builds directly on that SRC method, so all evidence is one group's work; a22 a19 a20 c17 are the same paper.

claim: A learned sleep cycle over the KV cache resolves proactive interference in a 793K-parameter toy transformer (99.5 percent at depth 5; 97.0 at 10; 73.5 at 15; 16.5 at 30; re-checked). Preprint, synthetic.
agent_test: Needs architecture training; for a scaffold, test explicit conflict-tagging and eviction of superseded facts instead.

claim: Fast/slow complementary learning systems with replay are a sound design principle for AI, backed by theory and continual-learning results.
agent_test: Fast store plus slow rule store versus single store, at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Training-based sleep (distilling into weights, RL-made dreaming) beats SFT and GRPO by 1 to 3 points on AIME/HMMT (Qwen3-8B AIME-24 79.2 vs 76.6, re-checked).
agent_test: Out of scope for a no-training scaffold; margins small, no seed variance.

claim: Reflection and rule-edit loops (Generative Agents, ExpeL) are an LLM analogue of schema formation and help agents. Caveat: in Auto-Dreamer's bootstrap CIs, ExpeL scored 28.33 vs 28.69 for no memory on ScienceWorld and 33.59 vs 30.83 on ALFWorld, so the help is not general.
agent_test: Rule list edited ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE from success-failure comparisons versus retrieval-only at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study tests human-style active-systems effects (spindle coupling, SO timing, stage dependence); all borrow the metaphor.
agent_test: Gap search to confirm; do not claim biological validation of any LLM design.

claim: No memory-agent paper read charges the offline pass's tokens against an equal-total-token baseline. Auto-Dreamer reports no consolidator tokens in its tables; All-Mem matches query-time budget with Mem0 but its offline pass costs 1,237 tokens/turn amortized vs 539 online; only RecMem counts construction tokens (193.2K vs 1,520.8K for Mem0), and there a full-context run still beats it on LoCoMo (90.84 vs 86.92, GPT-4.1-mini).
agent_test: Arm A: offline pass of N tokens then answer. Arm B: same N tokens spent as extra retrieval or extra reasoning at query time. Arm C: no-memory. Same tasks, 3+ seeds, report total tokens.

claim: Wagner 2004 exact numbers: Experiment 1, 106 recruited; sleep group 13/22 (59 percent) found the hidden rule vs 5/22 (22.7 percent) or 5/20 (25 percent) in each of four control groups; chi2 = 10.2, df 4, p = .03. Base rate without sleep is about 20-25 percent.
agent_test: None needed; use only as the human anchor for how small the founding rule-discovery cells were.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Which sleep stage drives rule discovery is unsettled: N1 in one nap study (N 103; 83 vs 30 percent), N2 in a preregistered one (N 90 enrolled, 68 analysed; 85.7 vs 55.5 percent wake, N1 63.6 percent not different), and nulls in others. No large direct replication of Wagner 2004 was found; the largest related studies are N 103, 90, 77 and 72.
agent_test: Do not encode a stage rule into the schema; compare a strict-replay pass with a looser free-association pass on rule-finding tasks.

claim: In an LLM consolidator, the number of episodes per offline pass has an inverted-U effect: Auto-Dreamer cadence k=1 and k=20 both underperformed the main setting on ScienceWorld (k=10), ALFWorld varied about 5 pp (k=5 was +1.1 pp). Authors attribute k=20 to a larger noisier region straining the consolidator's context. Only figure-level data; no seeds.
agent_test: Run the consolidation pass on batches of 5, 10, 20, 40 episodes at the same total episodes; plot rule quality and downstream success per batch size, 3 seeds.

claim: Deduplication is safe; summarizing clusters is not. On LongMemEval S-tier, dedup-only scored 76.8 [73.0, 80.4] vs raw RAG 78.4 [74.8, 82.0], while aggressive cluster-merge scored 48.4 [44.0, 52.8] (single-session assistant 94.6 to 39.3). But All-Mem found removing its Merge operator lowered F1 by 3.16 points (52.18 to 49.02), so merge helps when raw units stay recoverable.
agent_test: Ablation at fixed tokens: dedup only, dedup plus abstraction, abstraction with raw kept, abstraction with raw deleted.

claim: Keeping source-linked raw episodes protects against abstraction loss: RecMem without its raw-interaction tier fell 81.10 to 51.88; All-Mem without recovery links fell 52.18 to 50.06 F1 (anchors-only 49.27); a hand audit of 190 All-Mem edits found 94.2 percent valid and 3.7 percent harmful, with 0 percent of archived units unreachable (median 2 hops).
agent_test: Store rules with pointers to source episodes and let the agent open them on demand; compare with rules-only at equal tokens on date, place and number questions.
audit_note: All numbers match; effect sizes differ greatly (-29 points RecMem vs -2.1 F1 All-Mem, no CIs) and the 'raw tier' removal also removes the faithful-detail layer, so 'protects against abstraction loss' is an interpretation.

claim: Acoustic slow-wave stimulation evidence is weaker than the original papers suggested: the 2021 meta-analysis found g = 0.25 (p = 0.07, 10 studies, 177 people); the 2022 meta-analysis that reported g = 0.68 in under-35s was retracted (notice online June 2025, in the February 2026 issue) for using SE as SD and wrong sample sizes; closed-loop stimulation was null for memory in chronic insomnia (N 27) and at home (N 34, authors flag low power); and a tDCS plus CLAS study (N 20) was null overall, with a memory decrement only in an exploratory high-fluid-intelligence subgroup.
agent_test: None; do not cite stimulation results as biological validation of an agent design.
audit_note: Retraction notice of Stanyer et al. 2022 was first published online 16 June 2025 (it sits in the Feb 2026 issue, vol 35 no 1), not 'in 2026'; all other numbers (g=0.25 p=0.07 10 studies 177; g=0.68; N=27; N=34; N=20) match.
claim_before_audit: Acoustic slow-wave stimulation evidence is weaker than the original papers suggested: 2021 meta-analysis g = 0.25 (p = 0.07, 10 studies, 177 people); the 2022 meta-analysis with g = 0.68 was retracted in 2026 (SE used for SD, wrong sample sizes); nulls in chronic insomnia (N 27) and at home (N 34); a tDCS plus CLAS study (N 20) was null overall.

claim: Not found in any source read (search budget ran out, so absence is weak): an LLM study that measures false or hallucinated rules from a consolidation pass (DRM-like), tests schema-consistent vs schema-inconsistent integration, or compares hub/surprise/reward-prioritised replay with uniform replay. The nearest items are All-Mem's edit audit (3.7 percent harmful) and RecMem's recurrence gating.
agent_test: Build these three tests ourselves: planted-false-rule rate, fits-the-rule vs breaks-the-rule fact insertion, and prioritised vs uniform replay at equal tokens.
